The flaw,  CVE-2026-112900 , is in the way Pillow handles EPS images, which it opens by passing the file's name to Ghostscript , a separate program it runs to turn the image into pixels, without checking the name first.   Ghostscript can read a name chosen by an attacker as instructions rather than as a file, and point it to a second file that carries commands to run.
